issues.summary: Blueprint and ADR-0058 enumerate the 'three pre-existing event types' as {primary_degraded, readiness_probe, structured_failure}, but the actual on-disk vocabulary is {install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure} per OP-7 and postCreate.sh.

evidence.location: frontmatter `change_summary`; §Background and Context (ADR-0037 row); §NFR-13 prose; §AC-X-2; Interface Change Matrix (ADR-0037 row); §Data Flow; §State Transitions; §References — Inherited ADRs (ADR-0037 row)
§Context (line 43); §Decision (line 56); §Rationale item 1
REQUIRED_FIELDS dict (lines 23-29) — lists `install_complete`, `readiness_probe`, `structured_failure`; no `primary_degraded`
lines 70-184 — writes `install_complete` records exclusively for the install phase; no `primary_degraded` is ever emitted
lines 30-90 — documents `install_complete`, `readiness_probe`, `structured_failure`; `primary_degraded` appears only as a sub-field of structured_failure
line 23 verbatim: 'schema includes a `structured_failure` event type with a `primary_degraded` sub-field' — confirming primary_degraded is a field, not a type
live records show only install_complete / readiness_probe / structured_failure events; primary_degraded appears only as a boolean sub-field of structured_failure

issues.explanation: ADR-0037's prose (line 54) names the three event types as `primary_degraded | readiness_probe | structured_failure`. That prose is itself inconsistent with ADR-0037's own OP-7 implementation, which validates `install_complete | readiness_probe | structured_failure`. The Blueprint v2 and the newly-authored ADR-0058 reproduce ADR-0037's prose trio verbatim. The carry-through is at least eight places in Blueprint v2 (frontmatter, NFR-13, AC-X-2, Interface Change Matrix, Data Flow, etc.) and three places in ADR-0058. The propagation matters because the Plan author is directed (per Blueprint Implementation Plan step 11 and Step 6) to update `KB-mcp-design/references/principles.md` and `KB-mcp-platform/references/mcp-events-jsonl.md` 'to document the four-type vocabulary per ADR-0058' — but the Blueprint's enumeration of the existing three is the wrong trio. The mcp-events-jsonl.md file already documents the correct trio (install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure); a Plan-author working from the Blueprint v2's enumeration could mistakenly demote install_complete and promote primary_degraded.
issues.blast_radius_check: Affected surfaces: Plan-task edits to KB-mcp-design/references/principles.md (currently lists `primary_degraded schema-level provision` per line 58 — already inconsistent with OP-7), KB-mcp-platform/references/mcp-events-jsonl.md (currently lists the correct trio), audit_op7_events_schema.py (would need extension to admit `calibration_result` and possibly also reconcile the stated-vs-actual trio). FR-4b script emits `calibration_result` which OP-7 currently rejects as `unknown event type` (MAJOR finding per the script's logic). Until OP-7 is extended in the Plan, every FR-4b event would generate an OP-7 MAJOR finding.
issues.recommended_resolution: Two-part fix. (a) Plan Authoring task: in addition to documenting `calibration_result` in KB-mcp-design/references/principles.md, extend audit_op7_events_schema.py's `REQUIRED_FIELDS` dict to admit `calibration_result` with its required fields per ADR-0058's canonical payload — otherwise FR-4b events generate OP-7 MAJOR findings on every emission. (b) Reconciliation: either (i) treat the Blueprint's enumeration `{primary_degraded, readiness_probe, structured_failure}` as faithful-to-ADR-0037-prose and acknowledge inline that the actual on-disk vocabulary at the schema-validation surface is `{install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure}` (the ADR-0037-vs-OP-7 divergence is pre-existing and not introduced by this feature); OR (ii) correct the enumeration in Blueprint v2 §NFR-13, §AC-X-2, Interface Change Matrix, Data Flow, and ADR-0058's Context / Decision / Rationale to read `{install_complete, readiness_probe, structured_failure}` and note that the prior ADR-0037 prose's `primary_degraded` is a sub-field of `structured_failure`, not a distinct type. Option (b)(ii) is cleaner because it removes the documentation-vs-realization drift this feature's whole rationale is built to prevent. Reconcile with `finalize-reconciler` choosing between (i) and (ii).

issues.summary: Blueprint v2 and ADR-0058 repeatedly cite 'OP-6 audit rule' as the rule that 'rejects ad-hoc fields' or 'validates the embedded shape' — but the actual schema-conformance rule is OP-7. OP-6 audits runtime-log redaction (credential scanning).

evidence.location: §Background and Context (ADR-0037 row); §Architecture Overview block discussing closed-enum; §Interface Change Matrix (ADR-0037 → ADR-0058 row); §Data Representation Decision table
§Context line 43, §Why this in Decision Details, §Rationale item 1 (line 74), Options Considered Option 1 cons, §Consequences (line 119), §Implementation Guidance final bullet
§Architecture Impact item 4 (line 136) — 'ad-hoc fields are rejected by the OP-6 audit rule' (this is the original source of the confusion; Blueprint v2 and ADR-0058 inherit the error)
header comment lines 1-15 — OP-6 scans for credential-shaped substrings in the JSONL; it does not validate event-type vocabulary
header comment lines 1-15 — OP-7 verifies each line conforms to ADR-0037 schema; OP-7 is the rule that admits or rejects event types

issues.explanation: ADR-0037 itself misnames the rule (`OP-6 audit rule` for schema conformance) when the actual implementation is `OP-7`. Blueprint v2 and the newly-authored ADR-0058 propagate the error. Because ADR-0058 explicitly invokes 'OP-6 audit rule discipline' as the discipline-preserving property of the additive extension, the citation matters: the discipline preserved is OP-7's schema-validation, not OP-6's redaction-integrity. A reader of ADR-0058 looking for the audit rule that validates `calibration_result`'s shape would land in the wrong script.
issues.blast_radius_check: Affected surfaces: ADR-0058 §Implementation Guidance final bullet directs the Plan author 'OP-6 audit rule discipline applies: any record in mcp-events.jsonl whose event: field is calibration_result MUST conform to the canonical payload shape; ad-hoc fields are rejected.' A Plan author following this guidance literally would extend OP-6's redaction scanner with payload-shape validation — wrong rule.
issues.recommended_resolution: Correct every Blueprint v2 and ADR-0058 reference from 'OP-6 audit rule' to 'OP-7 audit rule' when speaking of schema/vocabulary discipline. Acknowledge that ADR-0037's original prose item 4 inherits the same confusion (a pre-existing project-level issue, not introduced by this feature) and either (a) note the inheritance and leave the error in the prose alongside the corrected reference, or (b) flag for a follow-on ADR amendment to ADR-0037 (out-of-scope for this feature per the carve-out, but worth surfacing as a deferral). The latter is cleaner; the former is feasible without a scope expansion.

issues.summary: FR-3 OP-11 audit's day-one false-positive analysis only addresses `mcp-openapi-schema` (row 71). ADR-0041 row 70 (Serena) still names `uvx --from "git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@${SERENA_REF}" serena start-mcp-server` as the invocation, but `.mcp.json` runs Serena via `command: "serena", args: ["start-mcp-server"]` (the installed binary). Under the Blueprint's canonicalize+opaque-tokens algorithm, this is a second drift the audit will surface.

evidence.location: row 70 — `Serena | uvx --from (Python; uv-managed; ephemeral) | uvx --from "git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@${SERENA_REF}" serena start-mcp-server`
lines 28-31 — `serena: { command: "serena", args: ["start-mcp-server"] }`
line 82 — `uv tool install -p 3.13 "serena-agent==${SERENA_VERSION}" --prerelease=allow` (binary install, not ephemeral `uvx --from`)
§Background and Context (ADR-0041 row) — 'This Blueprint annotates row 71 (mcp-openapi-schema) with [DEPRECATED — removed 2026-05-24]'; only ONE row marked

issues.explanation: The synthesis (§4 Notable Structural Findings, third bullet) verifies the mcp-openapi-schema drift and supplies it as the day-one false-positive trigger. Synthesis does NOT verify the Serena row 70 drift, but the live state on disk is unambiguous: ADR-0041 row 70 documents `uvx --from git+...` form; `.mcp.json` documents the installed binary form (`command: "serena"`). The Blueprint's FR-3 algorithm specification ('canonicalize whitespace + treat ${VAR} placeholders as opaque tokens + string-equal') applied to the Form column of row 70 versus the `.mcp.json` invocation does not produce a match — distinct command verbs, distinct arg shape. Under the Blueprint's design, this is either (a) a second `[DEPRECATED]`-marker candidate, (b) a row that needs ADR-0041 amendment (out-of-scope per the no-ADR-edits carve-out), or (c) a row that needs the algorithm to special-case 'Form' column cells that mix install-time and runtime forms. Blueprint v2 doesn't anticipate the case.
issues.blast_radius_check: Affected surfaces: OP-11 audit (FR-3) at Gate 6 on first invocation will likely emit a BLOCKER for serena's row-vs-mcp.json mismatch. The Blueprint's risk-table row 'FR-3 false positives on .mcp.json shapes ADR-0041 didn't anticipate' is the relevant mitigation, but the Blueprint cites only the `mcp-openapi-schema` case as the false-positive scenario it solves.
issues.recommended_resolution: Plan Authoring task: before OP-11 ships, run audit_op11_adr_parity.py against the live `.mcp.json` and ADR-0041 (as the Blueprint's §Verification Strategy 'First verification target' already calls for) — if Serena's row 70 also produces a finding, the Blueprint must specify how to resolve it within the feature's no-ADR-edits carve-out. Options: (a) add an annotation to row 70 that says 'historical install form documented; runtime invocation is `serena start-mcp-server` from PATH after `uv tool install`' (annotation-pattern, ADR-0005-honored); (b) special-case the algorithm to split 'Form' column cells on `+` or `;` separator and check each sub-form against the appropriate substrate (postCreate.sh for install-time form; .mcp.json for runtime form); (c) escalate to user as a deferral. Recommend (a) for ADR-0005 hygiene + locality-of-truth (matches D-0005's posture on the `mcp-openapi-schema` row).

issues.summary: ADR-0057's framing 'no existing execution_mode field on checkpoint.json today' is technically inaccurate — the live recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md already documents the field (line 138) and the orchestrator already writes it (line 412). The intent of ADR-0057 (canonicalize the field as a first-class load-bearing surface for FR-2) is clear, but the prose framing overclaims novelty.

evidence.location: §Context line 44 — 'there is no existing execution_mode field on checkpoint.json today'

line 138 — `"execution_mode": "specialist-dispatch | parent-driven-workaround"`, lines 166-169 — `execution_mode — field semantics`, line 412 — `Parent records checkpoint.execution_mode = "specialist-dispatch"`
line 106 — `"execution_mode": null` (the field IS present in this run's checkpoint, currently nulled)

issues.explanation: ADR-0057 framed the field as 'being introduced' after Gate-1 reviewer feedback. The framing is honest about the AC-FR-2 *load-bearing* canonicalization need but is technically inaccurate as a description of the current SKILL.md state. The field already exists in name in SKILL.md prose and as a key in checkpoint.json. ADR-0057's load-bearing claim — that FR-2 needs the field to be inspectable and that the field MUST canonicalize the closed enum and write semantics — is fully sound; the framing flaw is in describing the field as net-new rather than as 'promoting from documented-but-aspirational to authoritative.' ADR-0057 was authored in Blueprint v1 and v2 carries it forward verbatim; the architecture audit recorded this as INFO/recommended rather than important because it doesn't break any downstream consumer and ADR-0057 cleared review at Blueprint v1.
issues.blast_radius_check: Negligible — no downstream consumer reads ADR-0057's prose for behavior. The decision content (enum, writer, reader, absence-default rule) is correct.
issues.recommended_resolution: Optional and low-priority: at next ADR-0057 revision opportunity (e.g., a future feature that adds an enum value), reword the Context to 'The execution_mode field is documented in the orchestrator's checkpoint schema (recipe-feature-pipeline/SKILL.md:138) but is not yet a load-bearing audit surface; this ADR canonicalizes the field as the FR-2 dispatch-self-check inspection surface.' No change needed within this feature's scope; flagged for future ADR maintenance.

issues.summary: The Blueprint v2's FR-4 reshape rationale is honored throughout (FR-4a static-only sub-100ms; FR-4b behavioral on cadence; FR-4c CI wiring; Q-CS-1b banner as belt-and-suspenders). One minor clarity gap: the Q-CS-1b banner's 'NEVER RUN' variant is informational on first rebuild after this feature ships — which is expected and not a defect — but the Blueprint doesn't flag this expected-state-at-deploy posture to the Plan author.

evidence.location: §Cross-Layer ACs AC-X-4 — the banner emits 'NEVER RUN' if no `calibration_result` event has ever been recorded; §Data Flow Q-CS-1b block emits the same
§Verification Strategy First verification target (FR-4b smoke) — the verification target writes the first `calibration_result` event, which retires the 'NEVER RUN' state

issues.explanation: On deploy, the first devcontainer rebuild for any operator will produce a 'NEVER RUN' banner (no calibration_result events on disk yet). The Verification Strategy plan to run the FR-4b smoke as 'Second verification target' writes the first event and retires the banner. This is correct and intentional. The Plan author should be told to schedule the FR-4b smoke immediately on first deploy so the banner doesn't appear on every operator's first rebuild post-merge. The Blueprint doesn't make this sequencing concern explicit.
issues.blast_radius_check: Operator-experience surface only. Not a contract violation; not a blast-radius gap.
issues.recommended_resolution: Plan-author note (does not require Blueprint revision): add an ordered Plan task that the FR-4b script is invoked via `gh workflow run gitnexus-grammar-skip-calibration.yml` immediately after the feature's PR merges, before any operator's first devcontainer rebuild. This writes the first `calibration_result` event to the project's mcp-events.jsonl, retiring the 'NEVER RUN' banner from operator experience. The Blueprint's §Verification Strategy already supports this with the 'Second verification target'; the Plan task makes the sequencing explicit.
